Coverage gap, not a correctn…

### Architect (design / scope)
```

verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Well-scoped #2078 fix: Tier-0 mirror module follows docs-corpus precedent, cross-boundary rule pinned by dual (byte-identical + both-engine) parity tests, fails closed, both PR paths covered. No blocking design/scope/contract/DR gaps.
findings:
- low packages/minspec/src/lib/governance-transition.ts:governanceStatusTransitions — The absent/empty-patch annotation reads "(no patch available — treated as a transition)" while the workflow emits "(no patch returned …)" and "(patch could not be decoded …)". Cosmetic only — the reason string, not the gate decision, and it is outside parity coverage so the two can drift on this text. Non-blocking.
- low packages/minspec/src/lib/approval-pr.ts:laneRefusal — Introduces a second (TypeScript) definition of the lane's eligibility rule — the duplicated-predicate class a DR sometimes records. Acceptable here: it follows the established DR-less docs-corpus/ownership-path-rules pattern, docs-lane is not a required check (the workflow is an independent authoritative witness), and the change is reversible in <1 day. Observation, not a required change.

```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: Gate logic and parity are genuinely proven, but the new module header cites a containment test file that does not exist — a false signpost in a change whose own thesis is signpost honesty.
findings:
- blocking packages/minspec/src/lib/governance-transition.ts (module header, ~line 24) — The header claims the two pattern strings are "lock-step-pinned to the literals in the workflow by `tests/docs-lane-eligibility-parity.test.ts`." No such file exists — this PR creates `tests/governance-lane-eligibility.test.ts` (which `approval-pr.ts` cites correctly). A shipped source comment points a reader at a nonexistent artifact; the citation must name the file that actually contains the containment. This is the false-signpost class the change itself is meant to eliminate.
- medium packages/minspec/tests/governance-lane-eligibility.test.ts ('an unreadable patch on a governance path…' comment) — The comment asserts the annotation is "the workflow's own, carried over verbatim." It is not verbatim: the workflow emits `(no patch returned — treated as a transition)` (docs-lane.yml:202) while the TS/test emit `(no patch available — treated as a transition)`. The string is not a gate value and is not parity-checked, so behavior is unaffected, but the 'verbatim' claim is untrue and should be corrected or the wording aligned.
- info packages/minspec/src/lib/governance-transition.ts / tests — Verified as accurate (no action): workflow literals govern='^(docs/decisions/|specs/)' (docs-lane.yml:188) and grep -qE '^[+-]status:' (line 218) match the new constants byte-for-byte; DR-029/DR-086 §2 citations in user-facing text are correct; fail-closed and cap behavior are backed by real assertions; the two-witnesses claim holds because the client only withholds labels and the workflow re-verifies server-side.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

…gibility rule, so every approval PR was labelled onto a lane guaranteed to refuse it

Root cause: `laneLabelsFor` (packages/minspec/src/lib/approval-pr.ts) decided the
`docs-lane` label from docs-corpus MEMBERSHIP alone and never asked whether the PR
was ELIGIBLE for the lane. Since #1847 (docs-lane must refuse held PRs and governance
status transitions, landed 132a0bc6) the lane additionally refuses, with `exit 1`, any
PR whose diff changes a `status:` line under `docs/decisions/` or `specs/`. An approval
or acceptance PR is precisely that patch plus its approval sidecar, so it passed the
corpus check, earned the label at commit-on-approve.ts, and was then refused by the
gate. The gate that should have caught the mismatch is the producer itself: it had no
notion of the refusal at all, so there was nothing to fail. Verbatim, run 35783197257
on #2073 (SPEC-069 approval-record witness):

  ##[error]docs-lane: governance status transition in:
    specs/minspec/SPEC-069-approval-record-deterministic-witness/requirements.md

The same red sits on #2071 (DR-092 acceptance) and #2072 (SPEC-068 harness-refresh
direction gate). `docs-lane` is not a required check, so nothing was mechanically
blocked; the defect is a permanent manufactured red on the founder's own approval
artefacts, which trains every reader to ignore a gate.

The fix teaches the producer the lane's rule:

- New Tier-0 pure module `lib/governance-transition.ts` holds the two patterns as
  strings plus `isGovernancePath` / `patchHasStatusTransition` /
  `governanceStatusTransitions`. It imports nothing, so the question stays decidable
  offline.
- `laneRefusal` becomes the ONE lane decision and `laneLabelsFor` its label-shaped
  view, so the label and the reason it is withheld can never disagree. It can only
  ever withhold a label it used to mint, never mint one it used to withhold.
- `branchDiffEntries` supplies the evidence: one `git diff <base>...<head> -- <path>`
  per changed governance file, bounded, returning undefined on any failure. A missing,
  partial, absent or empty witness refuses the label rather than assuming the best
  (constitution invariant 2). An ordinary docs PR with no governance path needs no
  evidence and makes no extra git call, so it keeps the label.
- The toast and PR body now name the ACTUAL reason. The old text said "not docs-only"
  unconditionally, which is false for an approval PR: those ARE docs-only and are
  withheld because ratifying is a human act. A governance transition raises no warning
  toast at all, because it is the designed outcome of every approval and warning on it
  would be pure cry-wolf; the reason still travels in the status suffix.

THE DUPLICATED-PREDICATE RISK, and what contains it. The refusal is bash inside a
GitHub Actions `run:` block and the producer is TypeScript in the extension host, so
no artefact can execute both and one shared implementation is not available. Route
taken instead is the repo's established lock-step parity pattern, in
tests/governance-lane-eligibility.test.ts: it reads `govern='...'` and the
`grep -qE '...'` pattern out of docs-lane.yml's own text and asserts byte-identity
with the shipped constants, THEN runs both engines (bash ERE via the workflow's own
literals, and the JS predicate) over one shared fixture set so a dialect-level
disagreement fails even when the strings match. Verified by mutation: widening
`govern` to `^(docs/|specs/)` and narrowing the status pattern to `^[+]status:` each
fail both arms independently.

No workflow file is touched; the server-side gate is unchanged and still the
authority. Two independent witnesses, as before.

…im claim

Root cause: the module header for governance-transition.ts was written to
cite tests/docs-lane-eligibility-parity.test.ts as the file that lock-step
pins the two pattern strings to docs-lane.yml, but the PR that introduced
the module created tests/governance-lane-eligibility.test.ts instead - the
citation was never updated to match the file actually created, so it
pointed a reader at an artefact that does not exist. The accompanying test
comment separately claimed its "(no patch available ...)" annotation was
the workflow's own string "carried over verbatim", which is also untrue:
docs-lane.yml emits "(no patch returned ...)" and a distinct "(patch could
not be decoded ...)" for the two cases this test collapses into one TS
branch. Neither string is parity-checked (only the boolean transition/not
decision is), so no gate behavior was affected by either claim being wrong
- but a change whose own thesis is that signposts must not lie was
shipping two of them. Flagged by the Skeptic voter (ai-review:changes,
1 blocking finding) on this PR's first CI run.

Fixes the citation to name the real test file, and rewords the test
comment to say the annotation paraphrases the workflow's reason rather
than quoting it verbatim.
